doc.title: Fred Radke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Hillsdale, Michigan, November 8, 2023

title: Harry James and band singers
summary: Harry gave singers the first and last statements, found Sinatra, and had Helen Forrest and Connie Haines as singers.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: This is not a question but an observation. I watched a video of the band with you and took note of the song that had a singer and how the band played the tune and then it modulated for the singer. Not a question, I think it’s just an interesting thing, because I know it was fairly common for the arrangers to do that. And it was musically a good decision, sometimes a practical decision. The band sounds better in this key, the singer sings better in this key.

Yeah. Well the thing that Harry did that no other band did — see all the band leaders like Benny Goodman, Artie — they hated singers. I mean as crude as this sounds, this is how they used to think. Get a canary that looks good, put her in front of the piano so it dresses up the band. Have her come up and sing a few things. That’s how they thought, right? Okay. So if you stop and think about it, Benny Goodman introduction, Benny Goodman made the first statement, the singer would sing in the middle, and Benny Goodman would © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-

make the final statement at the end. All bands were that way except Harry. Harry thought why doesn’t the band play an introduction and the singer makes the first statement, I play the middle part, and the singer makes the final statement. He was the first one to do that. That’s like when he got Frank Sinatra. And you know that story, how he found him and wanted to change his name and all that. I tell that on the show you know, briefly. And so, and of course Harry James was the first one to do that. And of course his long association with Helen Forrest, everybody says, and I knew Connie Haynes who was his first singer, very well, and I knew Helen and did some TV and recordings with her. Everybody says she was the best. The best big band singer ever. And Sinatra said that too. And it was really cute, when we got ready to do the Fiftieth Anniversary show, and I did a TV show with her in Seattle and — did you know the Schribman Brothers?
